questions.q: Troisier's sign (enlarged left supraclavicular node) is seen in (GPSC Medical Officer, 2024):
questions.why: Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. Virchow's node.

questions.q: Aethusa cynapium is commonly known as:
questions.why: Aethusa cynapium is fool's parsley (Umbelliferae); wind flower is Pulsatilla, poison nut Nux vomica and bitter-sweet Dulcamara.

questions.q: A timid child who hides behind furniture when strangers come, and whose tonsils inflame and suppurate with every cold, needs:
questions.why: Baryta carb: bashful child hides behind furniture; quinsy and tonsillitis after every cold (Boericke).

questions.q: In chronic osteomyelitis, a piece of dead bone separated from living bone is called the:
questions.why: The sequestrum is dead bone; the involucrum is new bone around it; cloacae are openings in the involucrum.

questions.q: The last section of Boenninghausen's Therapeutic Pocket Book deals with:
questions.why: The seventh section, 'Relationship of remedies', is the doctrine of concordances.

questions.q: According to §138, the changes of health that a prover feels during the action of the medicine are:
opts: to be regarded as derived solely from that medicine
to be ignored unless they are new to him
to be regarded as his own latent disease
to be recorded only if confirmed in animals
questions.why: §138: all sufferings and changes during the proving, under proper conditions, belong to the medicine and are recorded as its symptoms.

questions.q: When two rubrics overlap, one large and one small, the repertoriser usually prefers:
opts: the smaller, more characteristic rubric if it truly fits the patient
questions.why: Topic 4, Repertory. Smaller rubrics are more individualising, but only if accurate.

questions.q: In Kent's Repertory, dreams are found in the chapter:
questions.why: Kent has no separate Dreams chapter; dreams are a rubric under Sleep.

questions.q: Intolerance of milk in infants, with the milk vomited in large curds soon after feeding, indicates:
questions.why: Aethusa's keynote is inability to digest milk, vomited in curds, followed by exhaustion and sleep.

questions.q: After which trituration did Hahnemann convert a potency into liquid form?
questions.why: After the third centesimal trituration the substance is soluble and is carried on as a liquid potency.
